sessions.phase_label: Initial question design, level structure, and Grade 2 curriculum
Level presentation, authoring-prompt refinement, and content revision
All-grade scope clarification and higher-grade content expansion

requirements.title: Curriculum-Aligned Content Across Grades
requirements.definition: Provide grade-appropriate Toy Factory topics and levels across the intended grades, with content aligned to curriculum progression.
requirements.boundary_note: Grade appropriateness and all-grade coverage form one curriculum-content obligation. Completing Grade 2 before moving higher is a work-order constraint, while individual level mechanics and presentation rules remain separate Requirements.

requirements.title: One Question Per Level
requirements.definition: Each game level must contain one question or exercise template.
requirements.boundary_note: This governs the number of questions assigned to a level, not the number of levels per topic or whether similar questions may be reused across levels.

requirements.title: Progressive Level Segmentation
requirements.definition: Split a mathematical skill into similar levels with progressively appropriate ranges or curriculum blocks.
requirements.boundary_note: The example ranges 0–20, 20–50, and 50–100 are parameters of one progression mechanism rather than separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Repeated-Question Spreadsheet Layout
requirements.definition: When the same question applies to multiple levels, reproduce it for each applicable level in the spreadsheet rather than representing all levels through a separate combined column.
requirements.boundary_note: This is an independently actionable delivery-format rule; it does not determine whether the underlying level questions may be similar.

requirements.title: Distinct Visual Representation Per Level
requirements.definition: Assign each level a different visual object and identify its representation type, such as an object grid, numbered box, or base-ten blocks.
requirements.boundary_note: Object uniqueness and representation type are tightly coupled attributes of the same level-visual mechanism; descriptions and objectives are independently editable content.

requirements.title: Level Descriptions and Objectives
requirements.definition: Provide clear descriptions and learning objectives for the designed levels.
requirements.boundary_note: This covers explanatory and objective text, not question count, visual-object selection, or curriculum topic coverage.

requirements.title: Sorting Activity Input Constraints
requirements.definition: Constrain sorting-activity content to exclude unsuitable arithmetic-operation problems, including addition, subtraction, and multiplication examples.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a specific independently testable content constraint for the sorting activity rather than a general prompt-engineering rule.

requirements.title: Reusable AI Content-Authoring Prompt
requirements.definition: Create a well-specified AI prompt that can automate content generation across grades and includes both desired outputs and explicit negative constraints.
requirements.boundary_note: This is an authoring-automation artifact used to produce grade content; it is separate from the C# runtime pseudo-random generator.

requirements.title: Constraint-Compliant C# Exercise Generator
requirements.definition: Implement the in-game pseudo-random exercise generator in C# so generated exercises obey their specified mathematical constraints.
requirements.boundary_note: Generating and reviewing question definitions before coding is sequencing evidence for this deliverable, not a separate generic testing or workflow Requirement.

requirements.title: Conveyor-Belt Player Interaction
requirements.definition: Describe the Toy Factory gameplay setup in which the player interacts with exercise content through a conveyor-belt mechanism.
requirements.boundary_note: The conveyor setup and its player interaction are treated as one tightly coupled gameplay mechanism, but the visible evidence contains only a freelancer implementation claim and broad mini-game scope.

unresolved_candidates.description: The client questions whether geometry, graphs, measurements, division, and fractions belong in Grade 2, but the wording does not conclusively establish the exact included or excluded topic set.
The freelancer proposes six to eight levels per topic, but no client response establishes a required level count.
A conveyor-belt setup and player interaction may be an independent gameplay Requirement, but no visible client message explicitly confirms the mechanism or its acceptance criteria.
